study type: Repeated Cross-sectional Study / Trend Analysis (Secondary analysis of two WHO multicountry surveys)
exposure: Robson classification (obstetric history, onset of labour, fetal lie, number of neonates, gestational age)
cohort: The study included deliveries from 287 facilities across 21 countries that participated in both the WHO Global Survey of Maternal and Perinatal Health (2004-08) and the WHO Multi-Country Survey of Maternal and Newborn Health (2010-11).
finding: The overall caesarean section rate significantly increased from 26.4% (2004-08) to 31.2% (2010-11), with women who had previously undergone a caesarean section being an increasingly important determinant of overall caesarean section rates in moderate and low HDI countries.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates increased across most Robson groups and in all HDI categories, driven by increases in induction and prelabour caesarean sections, especially in women with previous caesarean sections.
country: 21 countries (stratified by Human Development Index group: very high/high, medium, or low)
cross-section timing: 2004-08 (WHO Global Survey of Maternal and Perinatal Health) and 2010-11 (WHO Multi-Country Survey of Maternal and Newborn Health)
